models_evaluated: 11 LLM model configurations (not named in the abstract)

links.outcome: LLM accuracy under injected misleading context versus original questions
links.effect: Mean accuracy fell from 71.1% on original questions to 38.0% under focused misleading context, with 51.5% attack success across 11 model configurations.
links.quote: Across 11 model configurations, mean accuracy falls from 71.1% on original questions to 38.0% under focused misleading context, with 51.5% attack success.

links.outcome: Gap between licensing-exam-level scores and safe judgment under misleading context
links.effect: LLMs reaching expert-level exam scores abandon correct answers under misleading context; accuracy fell from 71.1% to 38.0%.
links.quote: We show this assumption is fragile: when misleading context is injected into questions that LLMs originally answer correctly, they abandon the correct answer.

unlisted_practices: Benchmarking epistemic resilience of LLMs to misleading or fabricated context in medical questions

screen.reason: Introduces MedMisBench, an automated adversarial benchmark to evaluate the epistemic resilience and safety of LLMs when presented with misleading medical contexts, but does not test an organizational deployment guardrail or practice.
